proof.text: First prove continuity directly from the covering-family hypotheses. The chosen covering pullbacks in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] imply that each covering presieve has pullbacks against every arrow. For a target sheaf G, preservation of pairwise pullbacks and preservation of covering presieves in [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor] identify the sheaf condition for the restriction of G on a source cover R with the sheaf condition for G on its image. For any arrow b into the target of R, choose the covering pullback family supplied by the source site axiom. Its generated sieve is exactly the pullback along b of the sieve generated by R, by the pullback universal property. The restriction is a sheaf on this family by the preceding argument, hence on its generated sieve. Mathlib Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff now proves continuity for the generated topologies. This uses only existence of covering pullbacks, not closure under every choice of pullback or strict indexed composition.

Translate the local conditions of [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor] to sieves: for source arrows a,b with equal images, the equalizer sieve contains the specified source covering presieve and is therefore covering in the generated topology. Likewise, the image sieve of any arrow between image objects contains the covering presieve on which that arrow lifts. Continuity gives CoverPreserving.of_isContinuous, so the pushforwards of both kinds of sieves cover in the target, giving Mathlib IsLocallyFaithful and IsLocallyFull. Each specified image-object cover is contained in Sieve.coverByImage, proving Mathlib IsCoverDense. Empty covering families are valid throughout.

proof.text: It remains to show that a source sieve S covers exactly when its functor pushforward covers. The forward implication is cover preservation. For the reverse implication, cocontinuity makes the functor pullback of the pushforward of S covering. If a:Y→X belongs to this pullback, factor its image as c followed by the image of some b:Z→X in S. Cover Y by the image sieve of c. On each arrow r:W→Y in that image sieve choose a lift d:W→Z; then the images of r followed by a and d followed by b coincide. Their equalizer sieve covers W by local faithfulness, and is contained in the pullback of S along r followed by a, since b belongs to S. Transitivity first along the image sieve of c and then along the cocontinuous lifting sieve proves that S covers. These facts furnish Mathlib Functor.IsDenseSubsite for the two generated topologies.

proof.text: Apply the proved Mathlib dense-subsite equivalence instance to sheaves valued in Type u. Its required right Kan extension limits exist because the categories are small in the same universe. Package the restriction functor as its asEquivalence. Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousCompSheafToPresheafIso gives precisely the required natural isomorphism with presheaf precomposition, including its action on sheaf maps. The statement is the same special-cocontinuous comparison used by its parent and preserves the proper-base-change unit route.

title: Special cocontinuous restriction preserves sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a special cocontinuous functor, meaning that it is cocontinuous, continuous, locally faithful, locally full, and cover-dense with precisely the covering conditions of [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor]. Then the associated morphism of topoi $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ is an equivalence. Its inverse-image functor is precomposition with $u$, so precomposition is an equivalence between the categories of sheaves of sets on $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal C$.
